issue.author: qa
issue.body:
Found on build 1 (game-developer 130237e4f3b0225bc25d661f98ee81d5fc6034b9 + sound/hit.wav 18f595a).

Steps: open `file:///<delivery>/index.html` in Chromium, press Start, click a mole.
Expected: point scored and the bonk plays (R1 'opens and plays in a desktop browser from the delivery'; R4 hit plays the sound).
Observed: score works, no sound ever plays: console 'Fetch API cannot load file:///.../sound/hit.wav. URL scheme "file" is not supported.' / 'hit sound not found'. `__whack.soundsPlayed` stays undefined. Over `python3 -m http.server` everything is fine (49 hits = 49 sounds).

The README says to serve over HTTP, so this is minor and does not block R1-R9. Possible fixes (your call): load the sound through an `<audio>`/`new Audio('sound/hit.wav')` element, which works from file://, or show a visible note when the sound cannot load. Report: world/qa report-build1.md.
issue.title: Minor: opening index.html from file:// plays with no hit sound (silent, console error)

comments.author: producer
comments.body:
Producer, for acceptance: I want this fixed before I approve. The release goes to a user who may well double-click index.html; a silent hit there breaks R4 ('plays a short hit sound') in the most common way of opening a small web game. Keep loading the delivered `sound/hit.wav` (no inlined copy): e.g. keep Web Audio over http(s) and fall back to an `<audio>`/`new Audio('sound/hit.wav')` element (cloned or reset per hit so rapid hits each play) when fetch fails. Everything else on build 1 passed my play, QA's report and the playtest; nothing else is requested. Please say in this issue which revision fixes it; I'll re-check it over both http and file:// and hand it to QA/playtest.

issue.author: artist
issue.body:
sound/hit.wav is pushed to world/artist main (18f595a): 0.25 s, 44.1 kHz mono 16-bit WAV, a percussive bonk, generated by tools/make_hit.py. Please put `sound/hit.wav` in assignment.json as artist's delivered path (assignment.json is missing at 4045fbb). game-developer should load it from `sound/hit.wav` on a hit.

For QA's listening.md: audio-understanding recognises it as a short percussive bonk but overestimates length (about 1.1 s for a 0.25 s file; the same happens for other sub-second clips I tried), so QA should confirm the length with `ffprobe sound/hit.wav` (Duration 0.25 s) as well as the model's answer. I have no other assets planned; the game can draw holes and moles with CSS/canvas. Tell me if you want sprites or other sounds.

issue.author: ht-admin
issue.body:
Make "Whack-a-Mole" as a small web game played in the browser: moles pop up in a 3x3 grid of holes for under a second each, clicking one before it hides scores a point and plays a short hit sound, and a round lasts 30 seconds. It has a title screen, the score and time left during play, and an end screen with the final score and a way to play again.

The hit sound is `sound/hit.wav`, made with code or ffmpeg: a short percussive "bonk", 0.15 to 0.3 s, at 44.1 kHz.

Before the game is accepted, the QA position hands `sound/hit.wav` to the world's `audio-understanding` resource and asks what is heard and how long it lasts, and keeps the request, the answer as it came and whether it matches the sound above in `listening.md` in its own repository.
issue.title: Game objective

issue.author: producer
issue.body:
What I need: (1) your systematic check of the assembled delivery against R1-R10 in `brief.md` (`ht-role brief`), with a report and reproducible defect issues in the owner's repository for anything failing; (2) R10: hand `sound/hit.wav` to `audio-understanding`, ask what is heard and how long it lasts, and keep in `listening.md` in your repository the request, the answer verbatim, and whether it matches the input (short percussive 'bonk', 0.15-0.3 s, 44.1 kHz).

The build: `ht-role delivery --into <new dir>` currently assembles game-developer 130237e4f3b0225bc25d661f98ee81d5fc6034b9 + artist sound/hit.wav 18f595a7f7373b331dd08c47c094d05136df8ed8 (also release `play-1` in world/producer). Serve the root with `python3 -m http.server`, open in Chromium. README.md documents `window.__whack` state for automated checks.

What I know: my own headless play with real mouse clicks at that revision saw a 30.01 s round, 39 appearances, longest 0.848 s, 34 hits = 34 points = 34 sounds, empty-hole clicks scored 0, end screen with final score, Play again reset to 0/30. ffprobe: hit.wav 0.25 s, 44100 Hz mono s16. The artist reports that audio-understanding overestimates the length of sub-second clips (~1.1 s for this 0.25 s file); record the answer as it comes and judge the match with that in mind, measuring length independently too.

What waits on it: my approval of the release. You also have no recorded commitment yet; please record one (`ht-role commitment --file`).
issue.title: Check build 1 against R1-R10 and record listening.md

comments.author: qa
comments.body:
Done, pushed to world/qa main (6f8ffcc): `report-build1.md` (R1–R10 table with evidence) and `listening.md` (R10).
Result on game-developer 130237e + artist 18f595a: R1–R9 pass in headless Chromium (30.0 s rounds, 49 clicks = 49 points = 49 sounds, empty/duplicate clicks score 0, max mole-up 887 ms, HUD/end/replay correct, mobile viewport + touch OK). No blocker.
R10: audio-understanding heard a short percussive hit ("kick drum/thump", then "bonk" when asked) but estimated 0.5–0.6 s / 0.9 s; controls (0.25 s tone → 1.1 s, 1.0 s tone → 1.37 s) show its duration bias, and measurement gives 0.25 s / 44100 Hz, so kind and length match by measurement, not by the resource's figure. Recorded verbatim.
One minor defect opened: world/game-developer#4 (no sound over file://; README already says to serve over HTTP). I cannot verify R9's 'generator kept in artist repo' (not visible to me): please confirm that yourself.
